Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagrnahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY 21 June 2006 PROVINCIAL DIRECTOR ROSARIO F. MAZA DILG-Region VI Fort San Pedro, Iloilo City Dear Director Maza: This has reference to your earlier letter-query in connection with the twelve (12) coun s of Dishonesty and Grave Abuse of Authority filed before the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) by t e Sangguniang Barangay members of Barangay Margubdub, San Remigio, Antique against th r Punong Barangay Aberto U. Villasor. After due notice and hearing, a decision was promulgat by the SB on February II, 2005 findihg Punong Barangay Villasor guilty for six (6) counts f such charges. He was suspended for 6 months for each count to be served consecutively b t not beyond his term of office. The foregoing events prompted you to seek our legal opinion on the following querie , which we reproduced herein in toto: 2) 3) 4) 7) 8) Is the conviction of (sic)6 counts legally right? Does the sanggunian has (sic) the power to render a penalty f suspension from office for the unexpired portion of his term? Is the decision tantamount to dismissal? If it is dismissal, is the decision n II and void? Does the decision needs (sic) a specific date for it to take its effectivi y since it was not stated in the decision? If the decision is null and void, can it be implemented? If the decision is legal, does it need a writ of execution for the punon barangay to comply with the decision? You also manitested in your letter that despite such decision, Punong Barang y Villasor still prepared the 2005 budget and was actually approved by the Sanggunia Barangay on August 26, 2005. On September 5, 2005, first-ranking Sangguniang Barangay Member Nerry Villanueva took her oath of office as Ac ing Punong Barangay. Villanueva ai prepared her own vesion of the 2005 budget. On September 8, 2005, the budget prepared by Viliasor was submit ed to an received by the Sangguniang Bayan for review. The budget prepared by Villanuev was also submitted to the Sangguniang Bayan. Up to the date of the letter-query, action, however, was faken by the Sangguniang Bayan. Villasor continuously presided over sessions of the Sangguniang Barangay un il September 9, 2005.

You again asked an additional query on whether the budget prepared by th Punong Barangay is deemed approved after the lapse of 60 days. We shall answer your queries in seriatim. In reply to your first query, we answer in the affirmative. An adminis ativ offense is defined as "every act or conduct or omission which amounts o, r constitutes, any of the grounds for disciplinary action" [Salalima vs. Gjngona (2 SCRA 56)). Given thif definition, a singie act committed by a public official, wheth r appointive or elective, is sufficient to constitute any of he grounds for dsciplina y action. Several acts committed by SUCh public official in several instances, one CT t separately committeci from the other, is su ficient to find him guilty for several counts f that offense. In the case of Padrones vs. Divinagracia (195 SCRA 675), the Supre Court found the respondent public employee guilty for two (2) counts of dishones y f r collecting money from two (2) complainants in separate instances and pocketed sai amounts. With regard to your second query, we again answer in the affirmative. Th Sangguniang Bayan may impose suspension from office, among others, as a penalty I an administrative case (Article 124, Rules and Regulations Implementing the Loc Government Code of 1991). Sec ion 66 (b) of the Local Government Code of 19 1 provides for the duration of the penalty of suspension that may be imposed, to wit: "SECTION 66. Form and Notice of Decision. — xxx (b) The penalty of suspension shall not exceed the unexpired term of the respondent or a period of six (6) months for every administrative offense, nor shall said penalty be a bar to the candidacy of the respondent so suspended as long as he meets the qualifications required for the office. (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the aforequoted provision, suspension as a penalty may be impos against a respondent local elective officia: eithe for the entire duration of his unexpir term or if he was found guilty for severd administrative offenses, suspension may •mposed for not more than six (6) months for each administrative offense. The Suprem Court held in the case of Salalima vs. Guingona (supra) that the Office of the Preside t committed no g ave abuse of discretion in imposing the penalty of suspensio although the aggregate thereof exceeded six months and the unexpired portion of th erring local elective officiai's term of office. The Supreme Court added that what s important is hat the suspension imposed for each administrative offense shall n exceed six months and the e shall be an express provision in the decision that th successive service of the suspension should no exceed the unexpired portion of th term of the office of the erring local elective official. Foregoing considered, we are of the view that the subject decision of th Sangguniang Bayan tendering the penalty of suspension against Punong Barangay s valid since all the requirements set forth in the Salalima case are me , as could b gleaned from the dispositive portion thereof, which we quoted as follows: "WHEREFORE, on the decision of all the members five (5) voted for the suspension. five (5) for acquittal of the respondent, as by substantial evidence, he is found GUILTY in six (6) counts of DISHONESTY AND GRAVE ABUSE OF AUTHORITY and is hereby meted the penalty of six (6) months suspension for each count of administrative offense to be serve consecutively but not beyond the term of office pursuant to Section 66 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991.'

By reason of the foregoing, further •discussion on your fifth query has becom As to your thiicl query, the penalty of suspension imposed by the Sanggunia Bayan against Punong Barangay Viliasor ha would last until the Fat er's unexpir portion of his term is not tantamoun to dismissal or removal. Athough both the penal y of suspension and the penalty of removal entail stripping off the erring ocal electi official of his functions for the rest of his term, there are other differences that distingu one from the other. Ihe penalty of removal from office as a result of an administrati investiga ion shall be considered a bar to the candidacy of the respondent loc elective official white the pena ty of suspension shall not. The penal y of removal considered a permanent in capacity while the penalty of suspension is only temporary As to your fourth and sixth queries, this Department has consistently opined th t after said decision of the Sangguniang Bayan was served to Punong Barangay Villas the Decision is already effective as to him and therefore, he is already legal y prevented from performing the duties and functions of his office for the unexpir portion of his term. No writ of execution or date of effectivity is necessary to impleme t the Decision of the Sangguniang Bayan suspending Punong Barangay Villas r. Consequently, the first-ranking kagawad Shail automatically assume the duties an functions as Acting Punong Barangay pursuant to Section 46 (a) of the Loc I Government Code of 1991 (RA 71 60) and shall thus perform the powers an responsibilities of the said office which includes the preparation of the barang y budget for the ensuing year. Anent your query on the preparation of barangay budget, Acting Puno Barangay Villanueva's version of the barangay budget for the ensuing year shoul prevail over the budget passed by Villasor, who was already suspended from offic Copies of said barangay budget a e required to be furnished to the Sanggunian Bay within IO days from its approval thereof. The review must be comple ed within 60 da s from receipt of the ordinance. If no action is taken within the said period, t ordinance is deemed approved (Section 333, Local Government Code of 1991) The fact that Punong Barangay Viilasor continued to discharge he duties an functions of the Office of the Punong Barangay (i.e. presiding over sanggunian sessio and preparing the barangay budget) during his supposed service of suspension, he said to be exposing himself to possible crim•nal charge of usurpation of functio punishable under Article 240 of the Revised Penal Code. In order to address fu ther the matter as to what possible actions to be taken enforce the suspension •mposed by the Sangguniang Bayan against Punong Barang Viilasor, said sanggunian should be advised to immediately furnish the Municipal May the Municipal Accountant and he Municipal Treasurer of San Remigio and the differ depository banks of Barangay Maragubdub, Municipality of San Remigio, of the Co of its Decision, together with proof of service. This action of the Sanggunian is expect to temporarily strip off Punong Barangay Villasor of his powers. We hope that we have addressed your concerns accordingly. Very truiy yours, W CELITO T.
